title: Rast wins Nürburgring Race 1 from pole as Müller’s jump start hurts his title bid
dek: René Rast won from pole by 10.787 seconds for Audi Sport Team Rosberg, and Nico Müller’s jump start and drive-through left the Swiss 47 points behind in the title fight.

chapters.title: A 20-point gap and a title that could end early
text: The DTM reached the Nürburgring on 13–15 September with the drivers’ championship down to two Audis. After 14 of the season’s 18 races René Rast led for Audi Sport Team Rosberg on 234 points, 20 ahead of Nico Müller’s Abt Sportsline Audi, with Marco Wittmann’s BMW third. Each race ran over 41 laps and included a mandatory tyre stop, and a weekend carries at most 56 points, so Rast could in theory settle the matter a round early, although the arithmetic made it unlikely. Müller’s task was plain: beat Rast on track, in qualifying and in the races, rather than hope for a mistake. He said he wanted no needless clashes between Audis, and that this was a circuit where a faster car can pass without great risk.

Audi had already taken the manufacturers’ title at the Lausitzring three weeks earlier, and Wittmann admitted that the marque had recently been collectively stronger than BMW. He hoped the Eifel would suit the M4 DTM better, and that BMW would be quick enough to keep the fight alive. Ferdinand Habsburg of R-Motorsport, whose Aston Martins had suffered reliability problems at the Lausitzring, said the team was working on set-up and engine performance. Mike Rockenfeller topped Friday’s second practice session for Audi Sport Team Phoenix, a hint of the pace in the Audi camp that Saturday’s qualifying would confirm.

chapters.title: Rast takes pole, but BMW breaks into the front row
text: Rast took his seventh pole position of the season with a 1m19.642s in the final minute. The surprise was Bruno Spengler, whose 1m19.822s put a BMW on the front row, 0.180s behind, in a weekend when Audi had been expected to dominate again. Müller jumped from the edge of the top ten to third in the closing minutes with 1m19.908s, 0.266s off the pace, and said afterwards that traffic on his quick laps had cost him roughly two tenths.

Rockenfeller was fourth and Jonathan Aberdein fifth for WRT, the Audi customer team, with Sheldon van der Linde sixth and Timo Glock seventh in the other BMWs. Loïc Duval, Jamie Green and Robin Frijns took eighth to tenth, so seven Audis filled the top ten. Wittmann was a disappointing 11th, 0.826s off pole, after finding Green on the road just before his lap and then running wide at the Mercedes Arena bend. Pietro Fittipaldi was 12th fastest but starts 15th on the grid.

Philipp Eng stopped on track with a gearbox problem and caused a yellow flag. He and Jake Dennis were later excluded from qualifying for illegal work under parc fermé conditions, and so start 17th and 18th. Ferdinand Habsburg’s Aston Martin stopped during the session, and Paul di Resta, 12th on the grid, was the best-placed Aston Martin.

chapters.title: Müller jumps the start and drops to the back
text: Müller’s start was too good. From third he squeezed past Spengler before the first corner, and it was clear that the Audi had jumped the start. He said later that the lights had stayed red for a long time and he released the brake to avoid stalling as the clutch bit. The drive-through penalty came at the end of the third lap and dropped him to the back of the field.

He stopped for his mandatory tyres three laps later, a gamble on a safety car that never appeared, and then struggled to recover ground on tyres that began to fade. Rast held the lead while Rockenfeller took third from Spengler at the second corner and settled into close support in second. Wittmann, 11th on the grid, was inside the top eight after the first lap. Spengler tried to take second back from Rockenfeller at the first corner on lap seven but ran wide, and the order at the front settled.

chapters.title: Wittmann’s strategy works, Rockenfeller’s oil leak ends a Phoenix run
text: The mandatory tyre changes reshaped the middle of the race. The Audis of Aberdein, Green and Duval stopped between laps 12 and 13, and van der Linde lost places with a slow wheel change. Rast and Rockenfeller came in at half distance, on lap 16, and rejoined ninth and tenth while four BMWs still to stop ran at the front. Spengler followed on lap 19, Wittmann and Joel Eriksson a lap later.

Wittmann’s late stop proved the best call of the day. He briefly ran third in virtual terms, then ran wide at the Mercedes Arena bend on his out-lap on cold tyres and let Spengler through, and spent several laps behind Green before squeezing past on the exit of Turn 1. Aberdein, Green, Duval and van der Linde fought almost all race, with Aberdein picking up scrapes with Green and a clash with van der Linde that damaged bodywork. Rockenfeller, running second, had felt the car sliding two laps earlier and retired with an oil leak after 25 laps.

chapters.title: Rast wins by 10.787 seconds as BMW claims two podium places
text: Rast was never threatened. He had built a gap of more than 15 seconds before Rockenfeller dropped out and took his sixth win of the season, 10.787s clear of Spengler, who ran a lonely second. Rast also set the fastest lap, a 1m21.358s on lap two. Wittmann completed a double BMW podium from 11th on the grid, 17.299s back, after a strategy that required no help from others and plenty of hard fighting with the Audis. Aberdein was fourth for WRT, matching his best DTM result, ahead of Duval and Green. Van der Linde was seventh and Eriksson climbed from 13th to eighth.

Glock fell to the back at the start and recovered to ninth. Frijns, who ran the longest first stint of any Audi driver, crossed the line tenth but was excluded after the race for using a tyre that was not assigned to his car. That promoted Daniel Juncadella to tenth, the one point of the day for R-Motorsport, ahead of Habsburg and di Resta, while Dennis retired. Müller was last of the classified runners, scoreless. Rast now led Müller by 47 points, with Wittmann 80 back.

facts.v: Nico Müller squeezed past Bruno Spengler for second at the start but had jumped it; he took a drive-through at the end of lap three and finished last of the classified runners.
